small_guidance:
- The kernel failed at the C launcher compilation stage (gcc subprocess error), which usually indicates an excessive number of kernel arguments or a launcher codegen issue. Reduce argument count by packing strides/dims that are statically known into constexpr (KD,KH,KW,OC,IC are compile-time constants from init), and drop unused params like OD/OH/OW.
- The inner loop iterates IC_KDHW=216 with full int divmod per element — hoist the (ic,kd,kh,kw) decomposition out by replacing the flat `kk` loop with explicit nested `tl.static_range` over (KD,KH,KW) and a runtime loop only over IC. That also eliminates the divmod and lets the compiler unroll.
- Add `num_warps=2` and `num_stages=2` autotune configs over BLOCK_OC ∈ {16,32}; OC=16 so BLOCK_OC=16 with num_warps=2 is likely sufficient and reduces register pressure.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as one program per (N, pooled-spatial-tile) instead of one program per N. With N=128 and pooled volume 7·31·31≈6727, a single program per batch serializes ~6727·8·216 = ~11M FMAs sequentially per program — massively under-parallel for a 4090. A grid of (N, num_pool_tiles) with each program computing a tile of pooled outputs over all OC restores parallelism.
- Use an im2col-style direct conv: each program loads a tile of input patches once, computes conv outputs for the 2×2×2 pre-pool window, max-reduces to one pooled value per (oc, pool_pos), and atomically (or via a second-stage reduction kernel) accumulates `(maxval/divisor + bias[oc]/PD*PH*PW... )` into a per-N partial sum. Then a tiny epilogue kernel finishes the global-avg + bias + sum-over-oc reduction.
- Alternatively, fuse only conv+div+maxpool into one Triton kernel producing a [N,OC,PD,PH,PW] tensor in channels-last layout, then do the trivial global-avg + bias + sum on torch (microseconds). This isolates the heavy op (conv) into a properly tiled GEMM-style kernel and avoids the deeply nested per-batch serial loop.
